Sk Afzalur Rahman, Advocate — For Petitioners. 
QA Hossain, Assistant Attorney-General ----- For Respondent Nos. 1-4.
parties:
Sk. Shahadat Ali and others ------------- Petitioners.
Vs.
Deputy Commissioner, Khulna and others ------------ Respondents.
full_judgment:
Mainur Reza Chowdhury, J.: This Rule Nisi under Article 102 of the Constitution was issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the -forcible eviction of the petitioners from 0.29 acres of land recorded in SA Khatian Nos. 1913, 1992, 1924, 1952, 1991 and 1912 corresponding to new RS Khatian Nos. 1807, 1887, 1819, 1847, 1886 and 1806 within mouza Boyra, JL No. 12 situate of Joragate under Upazila Doulatpur in Khulna Town on 28.2.83 should not be declared to have been made without lawful authority and to be of no legal effect and why the respondent No. 1 shall not be directed to restore the petitioners the possession of the same. 

 The petitioners along with 82 persons migrated to the then East Pakistan, 1947. They claim to have been victims of communal riots of Calcutta. An area of 3.66 acres of land out of 8.66 acres of land acquired at Doulatpur in the District of Khulna for the rehabilitation of the refugees was permanently settled with the petitioners and 82 fellow refugees for their rehabilitation. Out of the said 3.66 acres of land 0.29 decimal of land was recorded in the relevant SA Khatian Nos. 1913, 1992, 1924, 1952, 1991 and 1912 corresponding to the changed new SA, Khatian Nos. 1807, 1887, 1817, 1819, 1847, 1886 and 1806 JL No. 12 within mouza Boyra under the Upazila Daulatpur, District Khulna was permanently settled with the petitioner Nos. l and 2 and with the respective predecessors of the petitioner, Nos. 3-11. This land for rehabilitation for refugees requisitioned and acquired in Case Nos. 3/1951-52(5), 4/1949-50 and 62/1949- 50 of the Office of the Collector. Khulna. Since then the petitioners and others had been paying rent regularly to the then Government of East Pakistan and thereafter to the Government of Bangladesh. The petitioners and other refugees raised their homes and hearth on their respective settled land within the aforesaid 3.66 acres of land and have been in actual physical possession of the same. The petitioners and other refugees planted fruit bearing trees. While the petitioners were thus in possession of their lands, the petitioners along with other refugees were forcibly evicted on 28.2.83 from the said lands by armed police force. It is claimed by the petitioners that this forcible eviction was illegal, arbitrary and without any notice. The petitioners have annexed a newspaper report published in the Bangladesh Observer about the eviction of 50 families which was allotted to them vide Collector of Khulna Acquisition Case No. 4/49-50(4) in 1951 (Annexure 'A'). The petitioners were evicted from 0.29 decimal of land which they claim was settled to them and which they had been enjoying. The petitioner's right, title, interest and possession of the said 0.29 decimal of land was affirmed by the 1st Munsif, Khulna by his judgment and decree dated 30.4.66 in Title Suit No. 426 of 1965. In an appeal filed by the then Province of East Pakistan against the said judgment and decree of the 1st Munsif, the learned Additional District Judge, Khulna in Title Appeal No. 149 of 1966 dismissed the appeal on contest. Against the said judgment of the Additional District Judge, Khulna the Government preferred Second Appeal before a Single Bench of the High Court Division, being Second Appeal No. 395 of 1969 which was also dismissed for default on 27.3.75. Copies of the judgment and orders passed by the 1st Munsif, Khulna, the Additional District Judge, Khulna and the High Court are annexed to the petition in series and marked as Annexure 'B'. The petitioners have annexed rent receipts as Annexure 'C'. The certified copy of the land requisition and acquisition cases of the refugees of-the Collector, Khulna to rehabilitate the petitioners and their fellow refugees is annexed to the petition and marked as Annexure-D', The petitioners have also annexed certified copies of the first relevant SA Khatian Nos. 1913, 1992, 1924, 1952, 1991 and 1912 and certified copies of the corresponding changed new SA Khatian Nos. 1807, 1887, 1819, 1847, 1886 and 1806 and then marked as Annexures 'E' and 'F' series respectively. It is stated that although the petitioners' land in question measuring 0.29 decimal of land were requisitioned and acquired for the purpose of their rehabilitation and their title and possession having been recognized by the civil Court the respondents without any show-cause notice and without due process of law illegally and forcibly evicted them from their 0.29 decimal of land on 28.2.83. 

 4. An affidavit-in-opposition has been filed on behalf of respondent No. 4 stating, inter alia, that an area of 8.66 acres near Roosevelt Jetty at Khalishpur Bandar was required for the development of the aforesaid jetty and accordingly a prayer was made to the then Government of East Pakistan in 1954. However, the respondents admit that these lands were earlier acquired in LA Case No. 4/49-50(4) and 3/51-52(5) and the possession was made over to the Department of Relief and Rehabilitation for refugees from India vide Gazette Notification No. Khulna- 1047 Requisition, 8th February 1951. A copy of the said Gazette Notification dated 8.2.51 is annexed to the affidavit in-opposition and marked as Annexure- I. It is also stated that the petitioners were given allotment of quarters in the newly constructed Khulna Satellite Town, Khalishpur as compensation for their settlement but "in spite of all kinds of compensation and facilities given by the respondents to the petitioners families they tried to keep the property in their possession by illegal means and recorded their names fraudulently in the SA Khatian". It is also stated in the affidavit-in- opposition that "all attempts made by the District Authority to evict the petitioners from Government properties were met with failure because of false claims made by the petitioners in different courts". Ultimately, during the Martial Law, 1982 the District Authority by its memo No. 869 (BN)/RR dated 17.6.82 and the Chalna Port Authority by its Memo No. PCA/Secretary/Estate/Khulna/103/81-82-5058 (1-2) dated 14.7.82 filed a case against the petitioners to the Sub-Zonal Martial Law Administrator in the matter who by its order No. ML 279/815(2) dated 28.11.82/2.12.82 directed the District Authority to evict them and hand over possession of the same to the Port Authority on 28.2.83. Copies of the aforesaid Memos of the orders are annexed to the affidavit-in-opposition and marked as Annexures 4, 5, 6 and 7. The respondents have also appended the possession certificate being Annexure 10 in respect of certain CS Plots measuring 3.18 acres of land which were taken over on 22.5.72 for the Directorate, Chalna Authority in LA Case No. 1/67-68(4). 

 6. This fact has not been disputed by the respondents. It appears that against a notice issued against the petitioners to vacate their lands the petitioners filed Title Suit No: 426 of 1965 in the 1st Court of Munsif, Khulna. This suit was decreed in favour of the plaintiff-petitioners for 0'29 decimal of land appertaining to SA Khatian Nos. 1913, 1992, 1924, 1952, 1991 and 1912. The ordering portion of the decree reads as follows: 

 "It is an admitted fact that the plaintiffs are refugees from West Bengal and the suit land after proper demarcation by the officers of the appellant had been allotted to the plaintiffs on their application and this had been put into its physical-possession. It is also an admitted fact "that huts were constructed upon the suit land as on other similar lands at the cost of the defendants to rehabilitate refugees like they plaintiffs from West Bengal. There is no denying the fact that during the preparation of the SA Khatian the suit land has been recorded in the name of the plaintiffs upon assessment of rent. These khatians are exhibits 2 series. Not only that it is an admitted fact that the plaintiffs paid rent on the basis of this SA Khatian Ext 2 series and obtained rent receipts Ext. 1 series right from the year l961 which have been granted by the Government. All these facts are admitted by the defendants. If is the plaintiffs case that they applied for sanction of money to repair the huts on the suit land but sanction was not given on the understanding that the huts on the suit land have become the properties of allottees and as such they were to make repairs at their own costs. This fact has not been traversed by the defendants. 

 " After some years there accumulated some anti-social elements and started pilferage of food stuff in the Rooservelt Jetty. For effective stoppage of such pilferage and for security the Chalna Port Authority approached the Government for transfer of the above acquired land. The Government accepted the proposal and ordered for transfer of the land on payment of Tk. 4,80,000.00. The Port Authority duly deposited the money on 5.1.63 The Relief Department accordingly arranged alternative accommodation for the refugees in the nearby Housing Estate. But the refugees who were given possession in the Housing Estate were again returned to their original place after disposal of the properties allotted to them as alternative accommodation. These people even fraudulently managed their names recorded in the SA Khatian. The refugees and other anti-social elements jointly and separately started obstruction against peaceful transfer of the acquired land by filing Civil Suits one after another and obtained status quo/injunction orders from the Court Thus all possible attempts were previously foiled to transfer the-land and eviction of the unauthorised persons from the Government acquired land." 

 11. It will appear from the letter that the Deputy Commissioner had admitted that 8.66 acres of land in mouza Boyra JL No. 12 PS Doulatpur, District-Khulna was acquired for rehabilitation and accommodation of the displaced persons. It also admits that the names of the allottees were recorded in SA Khatian and that the Government could not evict those persons due to injunction orders from the Court. Annexure 6 the affidavit-in-opposition, is a letter dated 28.11.82 from the Sub-Zonal Martial Law Administrator to the Deputy Commissioner, Khulna which reads as follows: 

 13. It appears from Annexure 'F’ series and as has been stated by the petitioners in their reply to the affidavit-in-opposition that 0.29 decimal of land in SA Khatian Nos. 1913, 1992, 1924, 1952, 1991 and 1912 in Mouza Boyra comprise of SA Plot No. 3874, 6874, 6855, 6822, 6873, 3874, 3855, 3822, 3873 and 3873 as per Annexures E and F to the petition. 

 14. In the light of our above discussion and observation, we hold that the forcible eviction of the petitioners from their lands measuring 0'29 decimal of land in SA Khatian Nos. 1913, 1992, 1924, 1952, 1991 and 1912 corresponding to the new SA Khatian Nos. 1807, 1887, 1819, 1847, 1886 and 1806 being SA Plot Nos. 3874, 6874, 6855, 6822, 6873, 6873, 3874, 3874, 3855, 3822, 3873 and 3873 within mouza Boyra JL No. 12 under Upazila Doulatpur, District-Khulna Joragate District-Khulna to be illegal and without lawful authority. In the result, the Rule is made absolute without any order as to costs. It is directed that the petitioners be restored to full physical possession of their land in question.
